dimensions.name: Reference mining & contract inference

evidence.note: Viewed plugin-rsc types, plugin .d.ts, rsc.d.ts, and read the plugin-RSC README twice before building the plugin — grounding the Vite/RSC plugin API in actual type signatures rather than memory.

Substantial pre-coding orientation: test harness, fixture app configs, middleware/instrumentation, and both pages- and app-router fixture pages inspected before writing any shim; step 63 also read React-plugin types.

Sustained fixture consultation: viewed the relevant fixture page/test (blog, server actions, search form, server-only, SSR) immediately before implementing each subsystem — grounding shims in the fixtures being built.

No observed reads of /opt/reference/next-source/ or of any next-shims.d.ts contract file; Next.js semantics were inferred from example pages and test bodies (example-driven) rather than upstream source or declared type shims, and debugging re-consulted fixtures/tests, not source.

dimensions.reasoning: The agent clearly cleared anchor 3 and met anchor 5: it read the relevant Vite/plugin-RSC API surface via .d.ts files and READMEs, and grounded each subsystem in the fixture pages/tests currently being built, doing so consistently rather than just once. It falls short of anchor 8, however, because it never mined the vendored Next.js source (`next-source`) for ambiguous semantics and did not extract contracts from the fixtures' `next-shims.d.ts` type signatures — its Next.js contract inference was example/test-driven rather than source- or type-contract-driven. That places observed behavior at a solid 5, with only a partial reach toward 6 from the sustained-throughout consultation pattern.

dimensions.name: Subsystem decomposition & sequencing

evidence.note: Upfront reconnaissance of test harness, fixtures, and reference types, with TodoWrite at 27 and 41 — establishing sub-goals before coding rather than one undifferentiated push.

Scaffolding follows a genuine dependency-aware order: shims/module-resolution and plugin config built before router-fs/dev-handler, which precede pages-runtime, then app-runtime and server-action — resolution → server → routing → SSR/rendering.

Established a thin vertical slice: build+install+dev server, then iterated until a single route renders under dev (root match, second page) BEFORE running the full suite — the minimal end-to-end path from anchor 8.

Each subsequent subsystem (API, metadata, SSR, dynamic, forms, SSG/ISR, cache, actions, cookies) is worked as a milestone tied to a concrete failing test + fixture, but ordering is dictated reactively by the next failure rather than a re-planned milestone map; TodoWrite reappears only at 160 and 1246.

dimensions.reasoning: The front half exhibits clear anchor-8 behavior: subsystems decomposed and sequenced dependency-first (resolution/plugin → routing → SSR/features), with a real thin vertical slice (one route rendering under dev) established before layering features, and later milestones consistently tied to specific fixtures/tests. It falls short of a full 8-10 because there is scant evidence of an explicit, living milestone plan with articulated done-criteria (only four TodoWrite calls in ~1250 steps) and the long middle is reactive test-failure mopping rather than deliberately re-planned milestone boundaries, placing it at 7 — above the 'sensible order' of anchor 5 but shy of the fully dependency-aware, self-revised milestone plan of anchor 8.

dimensions.name: Test-driven verification design

evidence.note: Front-loads understanding of the verification harness: reads run_tests.sh/run_tests.py/filter.json, counts tests, and studies fixture apps and their test specs before implementing — establishing what the checks are.
Manually stands up fixtures (app-basic, pages-basic) and hits the dev server directly to observe behavior rather than relying only on the suite.

Fast targeted per-subsystem probes: SSR page, server actions/action state/redirect, and caching/ISR ('ISR cache MISS', 'STALE regen', 'RevalidatePath', 'unstable_cache') — verifying each subsystem's runtime behavior, not just compilation.

Minimal standalone-node reproductions for a hard subsystem (React error boundary / renderToString): 'Test boundary in pure node', 'Test renderToString', 'Test with constructor' — an anchor-10 style isolation move.
Root-cause interpretation: opens the specific failing test's spec/fixture to learn expected behavior before fixing, rather than patching the visible symptom.
Full Playwright suite run in background repeatedly across the run, interleaved with targeted probes and 'show failing' inspection — suite used as a periodic regression gate, not the only oracle.
Confirms the production build path ('Build vinext', 'Verify build', 'Prebuilt test', 'Final smoke test', 'Verify structure'), covering build in addition to dev.

dimensions.reasoning: The agent sustains a deliberate, layered verification loop across the whole trajectory: it studies the harness up front, manually stands up fixtures to observe SSR/SSG/action/cache behavior via fast targeted probes, and uses the full suite as a periodic regression gate rather than a debugger — fully matching anchor 8, including dev and build paths. It also exhibits two anchor-10 behaviors: minimal standalone-node reproductions for the hard error-boundary/rendering subsystem (steps 878-884) and root-cause interpretation by reading failing test fixtures (205-206, 402-405). It falls short of a 10 because the loop is predominantly suite-reactive with no clear evidence of probing behaviors the visible suite under-covers, placing it at 9.

'Test results before changes' — captures a baseline before a risky edit, showing deliberate regression-guarding rather than reactive fixing.
Extended error-boundary debugging where it isolates the failure with node-level probes and dev-log inspection instead of blindly re-running, then returns to the full suite (898-903).
Cookie-writes subsystem worked through many isolated probes and repeated full-suite runs; shows sustained tracking of one pending area to completion late in the run.
TodoWrite used only a handful of times — planning ledger is light; the run/failing-list test cycle, not a structured per-area board, is the main progress-tracking device.

dimensions.reasoning: The agent consistently runs the full 335-test suite after each fix cluster and enumerates the failing set and counts, giving it an accurate, continually refreshed done-vs-remaining picture and surfacing regressions across the whole surface — comfortably meeting anchor 5 and reaching toward 8 via its baseline-before-change check (712) and its habit of isolating stubborn failures with targeted probes rather than blind retries (803-896, 1116-1200). It falls short of 8-10 because tracking is driven by re-running everything rather than a maintained per-area pass-rate model, and the action index gives no explicit evidence of quantified area-by-area progress or self-declared loop-recognition.

dimensions.name: Design revision under divergence

evidence.note: Establishes the shim + plugin (router-fs/dev-handler/pages-runtime/app-runtime/server-action) + runtime-client architecture, which persists essentially unchanged for the rest of the run — the foundation is never fundamentally revisited.
Introduces a new node-resolve.js module mid-stream after dev-server resolution failures — a genuine adjustment to the module-resolution subsystem rather than a line patch.
Reworks CommonJS handling in plugin.js with multiple reads before edits, a focused subsystem-level revision of the transform/resolution path.
Full rewrite (Write, not Edit) of server-action.js versus its original write at step 126 — reworking the actions subsystem rather than hacking around it.

The bulk of the trajectory is run-tests/view-fixture/edit-app-runtime-or-client/retest, with dozens of targeted per-test Edit calls; predominantly leaf-level patching against individual failing tests with no foundational pivot.

dimensions.reasoning: The observable action arc is overwhelmingly incremental patching (anchor 3): a long loop of test-driven Edit calls to app-runtime.js, plugin.js, and the client runtimes, each targeting a single failing test, with the initial architecture never fundamentally reconsidered. However, it exceeds pure patching because the agent did rework several subsystems rather than only nibbling at leaves — adding a node-resolve module (150), reworking CJS handling in plugin.js (373-393), and fully rewriting server-action.js (672). This places it between anchors 3 and 5, without the deliberate, plan-updating foundational refactor described by anchor 8. Confidence is medium because the trajectory exposes only action descriptions, not the agent's reasoning about refactor-vs-workaround.

dimensions.name: Resisting overfit to the visible suite

evidence.note: Extensive upfront study of vendored plugin-rsc/next types, .d.ts, README and examples — points toward implementing to the real contract rather than guessing or hard-coding to fixtures.

Built a broad set of general next/* shim modules (link, head, router, navigation, headers, server, dynamic, image, script, document, config, app, og, cache, font) covering the actual module surface, well beyond the minimum any one visible test needs — consistent with faithful-semantics implementation, not per-test hacks.
Implemented genuine framework subsystems (dev server, build/start, router-fs, pages/app runtime, server-action, middleware-runtime) rather than fixture-specific stubs.

Persistent view-fixture -> edit -> re-test loops (dashboard, title-template, ISR, cookies). Legitimate verification, but the tight per-fixture cadence introduces risk of local fitting; no visible reasoning to confirm generalization either way.

File is an index of tool-call titles only — contains zero prose/observations, so there is no observable explicit reasoning about the visible-vs-hidden (335 vs 373) suite gap, preventing credit at anchor 8+.

dimensions.reasoning: The action pattern shows broad, faithful implementation of the real Next.js module and subsystem surface (wide next/* shim set, genuine routing/rendering/action/cache subsystems built from reference study), which matches anchor 5's 'implements actual semantics rather than test-specific hacks.' It does not reach anchor 8 because the trajectory contains no visible reasoning explicitly addressing the hidden-suite gap, and the tight per-fixture edit loops leave some residual overfit risk that cannot be ruled out. Confidence is low because the file exposes only tool-call titles, not the code or the agent's rationale.

rubric.task_read: This is a maximally long-horizon, high-complexity build: reimplement the core of Next.js (CLI, Pages + App routers, SSR, SSG, `use cache`, server actions, middleware, `after()`, client hooks, and a Vite plugin that shims `next/*`) as a single `vinext` package on Vite's plugin API, with no internet and only vendored source to learn from. Difficulty comes from the sheer surface area, tightly-coupled subsystems, contracts that must be reverse-engineered from vendored Next.js/Vite source and fixture `next-shims.d.ts`, and a moving target (335 visible → 373 hidden tests). A skilled practitioner would invest heavily and continuously in every meta-work faculty; ceremony risk is low, thrash-and-lose-the-plot risk is very high.

dimensions.name: Reference mining & contract inference
dimensions.description: Studying vendored Vite/Next.js source and fixture type shims to understand the Vite plugin API and the exact `next/*` contracts before and while implementing, rather than guessing framework semantics.
dimensions.why_it_matters: There is no internet; correct behavior lives entirely in the vendored source and the fixtures' `next-shims.d.ts`. Guessing Next.js semantics or the Vite plugin lifecycle guarantees rework across a huge surface.

anchors.0: Starts coding shims/routing from memory of Next.js without opening any reference or fixture file.
anchors.3: Skims one or two reference files or a fixture shim, then proceeds mostly on assumption; contracts are inferred loosely.
anchors.5: Reads the relevant Vite plugin API surface and the fixture `next-shims.d.ts` for the subsystem currently being built; grounds each `next/*` shim in an actual type signature.
anchors.8: Systematically maps the vendored Next.js source and Vite plugin hooks to the required subsystems, extracts precise contracts from every fixture shim, and re-consults source when behavior is ambiguous rather than guessing; notes non-obvious semantics (e.g. RSC boundaries, cache keys, action serialization).
anchors.10: Sustained, targeted research throughout the build: continuously cross-references upstream source to resolve edge-case semantics as they surface, distinguishes what the fixtures actually require from full Next.js behavior, and builds an accurate mental/written model of how routing, RSC, and module resolution interlock — visibly preventing whole classes of rework.

dimensions.name: Subsystem decomposition & sequencing
dimensions.description: Breaking the framework into ordered, independently-verifiable subsystems (module shim/resolution, dev server, routing, SSR, SSG, caching, actions, CLI/build) with a dependency-aware sequence and done-criteria per milestone.
dimensions.why_it_matters: The subsystems are tightly coupled and one package must ship all of them; without dependency-aware sequencing and explicit milestones the agent will build in an order that forces constant backtracking and never reaches a testable state.

anchors.0: Treats the whole thing as one undifferentiated coding push; no ordering or sub-goals.
anchors.3: A flat, generic list mirroring the requirement bullets, with no dependency ordering or done-criteria.
anchors.5: Identifies the major subsystems and picks a sensible order (e.g. resolution/plugin before routing before SSR/SSG), with a rough notion of when each is 'done'.
anchors.8: Dependency-aware milestone plan that sequences a minimal end-to-end path (one route rendering under dev) before layering features, each milestone tied to concrete fixtures/tests that prove it, and revisited as the build reveals coupling.
anchors.10: A living decomposition that establishes a thin vertical slice early, orders remaining subsystems to maximize how soon tests can gate progress, explicitly manages interfaces between subsystems so they compose, and re-plans milestone boundaries as integration realities emerge — never losing the through-line across the long horizon.

dimensions.name: Test-driven verification design
dimensions.description: Deliberately using and extending the Playwright suite and fixture apps as checks — running targeted subsets per subsystem, building smaller probes, and verifying behavior beyond just 'it compiles'.
dimensions.why_it_matters: The 335-test suite is the ground truth, but it is slow and coarse; verifying each subsystem needs faster, targeted checks and running the right fixtures, or the agent flies blind between rare full-suite runs.

anchors.0: Never runs the test suite or the fixture apps; assumes correctness from the code alone.
anchors.3: Runs the full suite occasionally as a pass/fail oracle with no targeted or intermediate verification.
anchors.5: Runs relevant test subsets / individual fixtures for the subsystem in progress and uses failures to guide fixes; verifies dev and build paths work.
anchors.8: Designs a verification loop: fast targeted checks per subsystem, standing up fixtures manually to observe SSR/SSG/action behavior, and using the suite as a regression gate rather than a debugger; confirms both `dev` and the production `build`/`start` paths.
anchors.10: Builds a deliberate, layered verification strategy — minimal reproductions for hard subsystems (RSC, caching, actions), interprets test failures by root cause rather than symptom, and actively probes behaviors the visible suite may under-cover, treating passing tests as necessary-not-sufficient evidence of a faithful reimplementation.

dimensions.name: Progress & pass-rate tracking across subsystems
dimensions.description: Maintaining an accurate, current picture of which subsystems/tests pass vs. remain, and detecting circular debugging or regressions across a very large surface.
dimensions.why_it_matters: With hundreds of tests and many interdependent subsystems over a long horizon, it is easy to fix one area while regressing another, or to loop on the same failure; an accurate done-vs-remaining picture is what sustains forward motion.

anchors.0: No tracking of what passes or what is left; works reactively with no sense of overall state.
anchors.3: Vague recollection of progress; notices only whatever failure is in front of it.
anchors.5: Tracks pass counts / which subsystems are done and which are pending, and re-checks after changes to catch obvious regressions.
anchors.8: Maintains a structured, updated view of pass-rate by area, watches for regressions when touching shared code, and recognizes when it is looping on one failure and steps back rather than retrying blindly.
anchors.10: Continuously reconciles a precise model of done-vs-remaining against real test evidence across the whole surface, catches subtle cross-subsystem regressions early, quantifies progress toward the full suite, and reallocates effort to the highest-leverage remaining failures rather than drifting.

dimensions.name: Design revision under divergence
dimensions.description: Revising the architecture or approach (module resolution scheme, rendering pipeline, cache/action wiring) when reality — failing tests or discovered semantics — contradicts the initial design, rather than patching around a flawed foundation.
dimensions.why_it_matters: Early architectural choices (how `next/*` is intercepted, how RSC/SSR is wired into Vite) will be partly wrong; the agent must be willing to refactor the foundation instead of piling hacks that make later subsystems impossible.

anchors.0: Barrels ahead on the original approach even as failures accumulate; only adds patches.
anchors.3: Makes local fixes when something breaks but never revisits an underlying design decision even when it is clearly the cause.
anchors.5: Recognizes when an approach is wrong and reworks that subsystem, absorbing the cost rather than hacking around it.
anchors.8: Detects when a foundational choice (resolution, render pipeline) is blocking multiple subsystems and refactors it deliberately, updating the plan and re-verifying dependents afterward.
anchors.10: Treats falsified assumptions as signals to rethink the design cleanly, weighs refactor-vs-workaround explicitly, executes foundational pivots without losing already-passing behavior, and emerges with a more coherent architecture — demonstrating sustained self-correction across the horizon.

dimensions.name: Resisting overfit to the visible suite
dimensions.description: Implementing faithful, general framework behavior rather than special-casing the 335 visible tests, given explicit notice that 373 hidden tests over the same behavior will judge the work.
dimensions.why_it_matters: The spec openly states the final grade uses a larger hidden suite covering the same behaviors; an agent that hard-codes to visible fixtures will pass locally and fail the real metric, so recognizing and countering this gap is a distinct, decisive meta-work demand.

anchors.0: Hard-codes outputs or narrowly special-cases the visible fixtures/tests to turn them green.
anchors.3: Mostly general but reaches for a fixture-specific shortcut when a behavior is hard, without noting the risk.
anchors.5: Implements the actual semantics for each behavior rather than test-specific hacks, aware the suite is a sample not the target.
anchors.8: Explicitly reasons about the visible-vs-hidden gap, generalizes each subsystem to the real Next.js contract from the reference, and avoids overfitting even under schedule pressure.
anchors.10: Systematically implements to the general contract inferred from upstream source and shim types, stress-tests behaviors beyond what the visible tests exercise to expose overfit, and can articulate why the implementation should hold on unseen cases of the same behavior.
